chunks: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmary from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Isma'il ibn Sahil from Hammad and Burayd and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: We asked them about the Zakat of Fitrah, and he said:

A sa' of dates or raisins or barley, or half of that of wheat, or flour, or suweeq (crushed grain), or corn, or salt, from the small and the large, the male and the female, the adult, and whoever is supported by him are all equal.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between these narrations, because the basis for paying the Zakat is from the surplus of staple foods, and each group of people gives what they consume as their staple food, even if one type is superior to another. And if that is the case, then mentioning the different types in some narrations does not contradict the types not mentioned in others, because they are restricted to those for whom that is their staple food. And the people of each land have been distinguished by that, as we mentioned, and all of that is on the basis of preference and recommendation. And if a person gives from the types we mentioned that is not what they consume, that is also permissible. And it has been narrated that the people of the lands are distinguished regarding the Fitrah.

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat of Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible food items and quantities for Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies that Zakat al-Fitr is not limited to the five specific grains mentioned in other narrations but is flexible based on the local staple food (quoot), a principle affirmed by Shaykh al-Tusi and Imam al-Hassan ibn al-Hassan. It establishes that while specific items are preferred, giving any common staple is valid, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of adaptability to regional dietary customs. This flexibility ensures the obligation is accessible and meaningful to all Muslims regardless of their geographic location.
